# W3: Journaled forward Mission repair with durable recovery

- REPAIR-1: API owns repair_preview/apply/journal/resume/rollback; thin CLI kebab-case commands and existing MCP mission_operation variants preserve the same diagnostics and results.
- REPAIR-2: Preview emits per-ID readiness/blockers, full-payload-bound candidate_overlay and deterministic planned identity, with no record, directory, journal or snapshot writes.
- REPAIR-3: Full-payload fingerprint covers sorted relative filenames and raw hashes for accepted/source, referenced Parts, history, projections and provenance. Apply accepts/verifies this fingerprint and CAS under the operation lock, excluding only explicitly operation-owned staging/journals.
- REPAIR-4: Apply persists actual durable journal and recovery snapshot before mutation, appends a forward authoritative revision, preserves historical bytes and merges accepted lifecycle/ownership with current typed prompt/Part meaning.
- REPAIR-5: Explicit no-op allocates no journal/revision. Partial set failure stops later IDs and reports persisted subset. Same-root journal read/resume/rollback use actual ID, revalidate last durable step and refuse corrupt/missing journals or later unrelated edits.
- REPAIR-6: Rollback is history-preserving operation-owned compensation, never whole-tree restoration or a synthetic historical journal. Fixtures prove same-identity repair followed by safe corrected typed rebind/publish.

## Failure and continuation
Stale Parts/history/projection must reject even when accepted/source JSON hashes are unchanged. Interrupted publish resumes only the same durable operation; uncertainty preserves evidence rather than replaying writes.
Apply common and per-waypoint branches from [outcome contract](../../../../../../transcripts/24-10-2026_mission-typed-authoring/OUTCOMES.md); after native binding that content must be embedded in the accepted Mission, not require this dossier at runtime.

## Validation and checkpoint
- `rtk cargo test -p mission --features cli,mcp --test recovery_move_contract repair_`
Focused selectors run once per owning changed revision, nonzero cases mandatory; no Python, active-denial machinery or unchanged broad final reruns. Planned guard `mission-recovery-repair` is registered/read back as execution evidence, never claimed run in planning.

## Scope and authority
Entity relocation, live five-record application during provider implementation, or restoring old snapshots over new edits.
Planning correction is not execution. Do not mutate live Mission/Session entities until the applicable execution and exact-set approval gates pass.
[Owning specification](../../../../spec/specs/44f100c4-215e-445a-b452-1a8a969d96cc/body.md)
[Detailed execution package](../../../../../../transcripts/24-10-2026_mission-typed-authoring/03-adapters.md)

## Test CLI verification failure: root cause

The `verified -> verified` error during automatic W3 spec verification is explained by a test-cli store-resolution mismatch, not by a W3 recovery implementation failure. `test-cli::resolve_spec_root()` appends `.spec` to the parent of the canonical test store. For `workflow-tools/.workflow-tools/test`, that opens the legacy `workflow-tools/.workflow-tools/.spec` index rather than the canonical `workflow-tools/.workflow-tools/spec` index. The legacy index reports stale state `verified`; canonical `spec get` reports the W3 manifest as `implemented` (revision 7).

Bug ticket `a7f9f4a0-ade7-4023-b45d-c6431a45de03` tracks correcting test-cli workspace resolution and adding regression coverage. This is related to, but distinct from, ticket `50092f61-f4fb-49a1-ac67-64c8cb7c513e`, which investigates a different ticket-MCP root-resolution divergence.

No W3 spec state or content was changed. W3 remains `in-implementation` pending its required review.

## Test CLI verification failure: confirmed root cause

The `verified -> verified` error during automatic W3 spec verification came from test-cli store resolution, not W3 recovery behavior. The old `resolve_spec_root()` appended `.spec` to the parent of the canonical test store, selecting `workflow-tools/.workflow-tools/.spec` instead of the canonical `workflow-tools/.workflow-tools/spec` store. The wrongly selected index had stale state `verified`; the canonical W3 manifest was `implemented` at revision 7.

Bug ticket `a7f9f4a0-ade7-4023-b45d-c6431a45de03` tracks canonical resolution, conflicting-store regression coverage, and idempotent spec verification. It is related to, but distinct from, ticket `50092f61-f4fb-49a1-ac67-64c8cb7c513e`, which concerns another ticket-MCP root-resolution divergence.

No W3 spec state was manually changed. W3 remained `in-implementation` pending its required review.

## W3 verification follow-up

- Test CLI now resolves the spec root through the shared canonical workspace/store helpers for both explicit and ambient workspace paths. It no longer derives or selects a legacy sibling path. Existing on-disk legacy data was not deleted or migrated.
- Regression coverage creates the same spec ID as `implemented` in the canonical store and `verified` in the wrongly-derived store, then proves the CLI updates the canonical copy. The path tests cover explicit and ambient selection.
- `cargo test --manifest-path workflow-tools/Cargo.toml --locked -p spec-api`: 99 passed.
- `cargo test --manifest-path workflow-tools/Cargo.toml --locked -p mission-api`: 41 passed.
- `cargo test --manifest-path workflow-tools/Cargo.toml --locked -p mission --all-features -- --test-threads=1`: 50 passed.
- W3 package evidence is recorded as `ae41c0ca-75fa-497e-b4ac-90e3fa04f6ec-mission-w3-canonical-root-fix-01`; linked guard evidence is `ae41c0ca-75fa-497e-b4ac-90e3fa04f6ec-mission-w3-canonical-root-fix-linked`. Canonical spec 44f100c4-215e-445a-b452-1a8a969d96cc now reads `verified` through the supported guard recomputation path.
- Full test-cli suite remains blocked by the unrelated existing `run_flags_over_budget_against_spec_threshold` test: its `echo slow` command measured 0 ms against a 0 ms threshold. It failed both in the full suite (16 passed, 1 failed) and as an isolated test. This test was not changed.
